Every kind of Parlour client sharing one server, one token and per-client sessions

nodes.label: Parlour (project overview)
nodes.author: Michael Parker
nodes.rationale: A voice assistant for your home that runs on a Mac you already own. A small local model handles the house; a cloud model steps in only when a question is beyond it and only ever gets the sentence, never the audio. MIT, copyright 2026 Michael Parker.

nodes.label: Dependabot configuration
nodes.rationale: Weekly and grouped so a quiet week is one PR per ecosystem (npm, cargo, github-actions) rather than one per package; major bumps get their own PR because those need reading. One npm entry at the root covers root, packages/parlour and apps/desktop because they share one pnpm lock file.

nodes.label: CI check job (typecheck, lint, test, build, cargo check)
nodes.norm_label: ci check job (typecheck, lint, test, build, cargo check)
nodes.rationale: Runs on macos-latest because the package's native dependencies (onnxruntime, the wake word and the voice) and the desktop app both build for it and it is the only platform the release ships for; Linux support would add a second runner, not replace this one. pnpm version comes from packageManager in package.json so there is one place to bump it. Runs pnpm exec nx run-many -t typecheck lint test build, then generates icons, then nx run desktop:cargo-check.

nodes.label: CI workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs on push to main, pull_request and workflow_dispatch. Concurrency group keyed on workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress so a push to a branch with an open PR runs once and a newer push replaces a running one. Permissions are contents: read only.

nodes.label: Build the app and attach dmg to release job
nodes.norm_label: build the app and attach dmg to release job
nodes.rationale: contents: write to create the release and upload the .dmg. pnpm -C apps/desktop build is pnpm icons && tauri build, and Tauri runs pnpm build:ui first through beforeBuildCommand, so one step produces icons, frontend, binary, .app and .dmg. Uses softprops/action-gh-release with generate_release_notes and fail_on_unmatched_files.

nodes.label: Publish parlour to npm job
nodes.rationale: Runs on macOS because the package's tests assume launchd and avfoundation, as CI does. Needs id-token: write for OIDC provenance. Tests and builds packages/parlour, then npm publish --provenance --access public.

nodes.label: Release workflow (tag vX.Y.Z)
nodes.rationale: Triggered by pushing a v* tag after pnpm version:set X.Y.Z and a CHANGELOG entry. The package goes to npm and the app to a GitHub release with notes generated from the PRs since the last one. Two independent jobs: publish and app.

nodes.label: Desktop app HTML shell (mounts /src/main.tsx into #root)
nodes.rationale: Minimal Vite entry: lang en-GB, a single #root div and a module script for /src/main.tsx. Built to apps/desktop/dist, which Tauri embeds at compile time.

nodes.label: Copy install command button script
nodes.rationale: The page's one piece of behaviour: clicking .install writes data-copy (npm install -g parlour) to the clipboard via navigator.clipboard.writeText, shows 'copied' or falls back to 'select and copy', and clears the note after 1800 ms. Everything else on the page is a link.

nodes.label: Parlour landing page (heyparlour.app)
nodes.rationale: Static page in en-GB with Young Serif from Google Fonts, an SVG favicon, light/dark theme-color, OpenGraph tags, and sections: hero, the speech loop, three pillars, Home Assistant, ten-minute start, open source, footer. Links to GitHub docs, releases, provider guide, contributing guide and npm.

nodes.label: Vercel Web Analytics shim (window.va queue)
nodes.rationale: Defines window.va as a queueing stub pushing onto window.vaq until the deferred /_vercel/insights/script.js loads.

nodes.label: pnpm workspace (packages/*, apps/*)
nodes.rationale: Single workspace covering packages/* and apps/*, sharing one lock file.

nodes.label: 'Made for Home Assistant' section
nodes.rationale: HA's MCP Server integration publishes what you have exposed to voice assistants as tools, so Parlour does exactly what you allowed and nothing more. A mute switch lives in Home Assistant rather than on the Mac so the house can keep Parlour quiet while everyone is asleep. Point the OpenAI Conversation integration at Parlour and existing voice satellites use it as their brain.

nodes.label: Three pillars: voice stays home, swap any part, one Mac every room
nodes.norm_label: three pillars: voice stays home, swap any part, one mac every room
nodes.rationale: Your voice stays at home (no account, no server in the middle, cloud only gets text and only when the local model decides); swap any part you like (each stage is a provider named in one config file, publish your own as an npm package and parlour doctor tells you whether it is happy); one Mac, every room (satellites find the server on their own: another Mac, a phone, a Voice PE through Home Assistant, or a soldered board streaming audio to a socket; automations get text in, answer out).

nodes.label: 'Up and running in ten minutes' section
nodes.norm_label: 'up and running in ten minutes' section
nodes.rationale: npm install -g parlour, parlour init (fetches and asks questions), parlour text (chat in terminal, no mic), parlour start. Needs a Mac with Node 22 and Homebrew; init fetches ffmpeg, whisper.cpp and the models, asks for the HA token, offers an Anthropic key, and can set Parlour to start at login. The menu bar app does the same things with buttons.

nodes.label: 'What happens when you speak' loop section
nodes.norm_label: 'what happens when you speak' loop section
nodes.rationale: Ordered list of the pipeline for the public: 'Hey Parlour' (openWakeWord on your Mac only), you talk (stops after 800 ms of quiet), words (whisper.cpp kept warm, under a second), thinking (local model with tools: house over MCP, timers, search, connected accounts), a hand from the cloud (Claude only when the local model decides), a voice (Kokoro, first sentence while the rest is made), your speakers or whichever room you asked from.

nodes.label: Community Impact enforcement ladder (Correction, Warning, Temporary Ban, Permanent Ban)
nodes.norm_label: community impact enforcement ladder (correction, warning, temporary ban, permanent ban)
nodes.rationale: Four escalating consequences inspired by Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder.

nodes.label: Coding conventions (strict TS, .ts imports, node:test, Biome, British English)
nodes.norm_label: coding conventions (strict ts, .ts imports, node:test, biome, british english)
nodes.rationale: TypeScript strict; relative imports inside packages/parlour/src use the .ts extension. Tests next to the source as *.test.ts with node:test and node:assert/strict, no test framework. Biome formats and lints. British English with no em dashes in comments, docs and CLI output; comments explain why, not what. Nothing secret in config: tokens come from secrets.env or the environment, never config.json, and are never printed.

nodes.label: Pull request conventions
nodes.rationale: One change per PR; say what it does and why; mention what could not be tested (e.g. a Linux change from a Mac). CI runs typecheck, lint, tests, build and cargo check and must be green. Commit messages are a sentence in the imperative.

nodes.label: Releasing (version:set, hand-written CHANGELOG, vX.Y.Z tag)
nodes.rationale: pnpm version:set X.Y.Z bumps both packages and the app; CHANGELOG.md is written by hand; pushing a vX.Y.Z tag publishes the package to npm and attaches the dmg to a GitHub release.

nodes.label: Development setup (Node 22, pnpm 10, Rust, parlour-dev)
nodes.rationale: The CLI runs straight from source with type stripping via packages/parlour/bin/parlour-dev, so there is no build step while working. pnpm -C packages/parlour build compiles to dist/, which is what npm publish ships and node dist/cli/main.js runs. The app is opened with pnpm -C apps/desktop app and drives whichever parlour its Settings tab points at (global install by default); set 'The parlour command' to the absolute path of parlour-dev to run the checkout.

nodes.label: Where things go (change to location map)
nodes.norm_label: where things go (change to location map)
nodes.rationale: New engine for an existing port: packages/parlour/src/providers/<kind>/<name>.ts registered in providers/index.ts, or an npm package. New tool source: src/integrations/<name>/. New port: core/ports.ts, a slot in core/config.ts, wiring in core/agent.ts, a fake in testing/; open an issue first because a port is a promise to every provider. Linux: a systemd service provider and non-avfoundation audio providers; core/paths.ts already follows XDG. CLI command: src/cli/<name>.ts exporting a Command, listed in cli/main.ts. The app (apps/desktop) drives the CLI, so add CLI capability first. The website is apps/site, one HTML file and one stylesheet.

nodes.label: The parlour CLI commands
nodes.rationale: init [--yes] [--no-deps] [--no-service] [--porcelain], start [--events], text, doctor [--json], service install|uninstall|restart|status|logs, connectors add|list|remove, models fetch, config path|show|write|edit, secrets status|set. connectors add signs the household in to a remote MCP server and keeps tokens in the Keychain; the connectors integration is on by default and doctor warns if a hand-written config leaves it out.

nodes.label: One server, any number of rooms (client topology)
nodes.norm_label: one server, any number of rooms (client topology)
nodes.rationale: One machine runs the models, holds the tokens and answers; everything else with a microphone is a client, and the server's own microphone is just one client with no special privileges. Clients: server mic (in process, openWakeWord); satellite (role: satellite, finds the server with Bonjour, holds a socket open, wake word on the server over the stream or locally with localWake); Home Assistant and Voice PE via the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint (wake word on device, HA does STT and speech back); a phone via the page at / with hold-to-talk (thumb as endpoint detector, phone not listening all day); custom hardware via the /listen socket with raw 16 kHz mono PCM; automations via POST /ask.

nodes.label: Getting started (npm install -g parlour, init, text, start)
nodes.norm_label: getting started (npm install -g parlour, init, text, start)
nodes.rationale: Requires a Mac with Node 22+ and Homebrew; init fetches ffmpeg, whisper.cpp and the models through brew, asks for the Home Assistant address and token and an optional Anthropic key, writes ~/.config/parlour/config.json and secrets.env, offers to run at login, and finishes with parlour doctor. LM Studio is the easy local model option; anything speaking the OpenAI chat completions API works.

nodes.label: Home Assistant over MCP
nodes.rationale: Home Assistant's MCP Server integration publishes whatever is exposed to voice assistants as tools, so Parlour can do exactly what is allowed and nothing more. The OpenAI Conversation integration pointed at Parlour's /v1 lets Voice PE satellites use it as their brain.

nodes.label: Kokoro (text to speech)
nodes.rationale: In-process voice on the Mac; speaks the first sentence while the rest is still being generated.

nodes.label: LM Studio (local model server)
nodes.rationale: The easy option for the local model; init offers to install it. Anything that speaks the OpenAI chat completions API works too.

nodes.label: openWakeWord (wake word engine)
nodes.rationale: In-process, always-local wake word detection on the Mac; runs on onnxruntime.

nodes.label: parlour doctor
nodes.rationale: Reports which of the moving parts is down, with --json for the app. Run at the end of init. The project's chosen substitute for unit tests on hardware-, model- and network-dependent providers.

nodes.label: Repository layout (packages/parlour, apps/desktop, apps/site, docs)
nodes.rationale: packages/parlour is the npm package (core, built-in providers, integrations, server, CLI); apps/desktop is the menu bar app (Tauri, React, a Rust shell that drives the CLI); apps/site is one page and one stylesheet; docs/ holds the pages. pnpm and nx; pnpm check runs typecheck, lint and tests across every project.

nodes.label: What happens when you speak (voice pipeline)
nodes.norm_label: what happens when you speak (voice pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Wake word (openWakeWord, in process, always local) -> record (energy endpointing, stops on 800 ms of silence) -> speech to text (whisper.cpp small.en, kept warm) -> the model (a local model with tools over the OpenAI API) -> tools (Home Assistant over MCP, timers, search, connectors) -> escalate (Claude when the local model says it is out of its depth) -> text to speech (Kokoro, in process) -> the speakers.

nodes.label: whisper.cpp (speech to text)
nodes.rationale: small.en model kept warm on the machine (io.parlour.whisper LaunchAgent) so transcription finishes in under a second.

nodes.label: Connectors OAuth threat area
nodes.rationale: The OAuth flow (loopback redirect, PKCE, token refresh), and a connector's tools being reachable by something that is not the household.

nodes.label: Installation threat area
nodes.rationale: parlour init, parlour models fetch and the app's npm install -g fetching from anywhere other than where they say.

nodes.label: Network server threat area
nodes.rationale: Anything reachable without the token beyond /health and the phone page's own files; any way to bind beyond loopback without a token; reading a file outside src/server/web through the page routes; one client's conversation leaking into another's.

nodes.label: Prompt injection via tool results or transcriptions
nodes.norm_label: prompt injection via tool results or transcriptions
nodes.rationale: A tool result or a transcription that can make the model call a tool it was not asked to. Hard to fix in general; reports with a concrete reproduction are welcome.

nodes.label: Token handling threat area
nodes.rationale: PARLOUR_TOKEN, HA_TOKEN and API keys must never appear in config, logs, --json output, the event stream, a process listing or the desktop app's window. Connector tokens belong in the Keychain or the mode-600 file store and nowhere else.

nodes.label: Bug report issue template
nodes.rationale: Asks for parlour doctor output and the log because most problems can be pinned down from those two; warns never to paste tokens since parlour secrets status reports which are set without values. The client dropdown enumerates every request source (server mic, satellite, Home Assistant/Voice PE, phone page, /listen hardware, /ask, parlour text, desktop app).

nodes.label: Feature or provider request template
nodes.rationale: Steers requesters to docs/providers.md first, because a new engine for an existing port can ship as an npm package with no change to the repo; issues are for built-in providers or ports that do not exist yet. Kinds of change mirror the CONTRIBUTING 'where things go' table.

nodes.label: Pull request template and merge checklist
nodes.norm_label: pull request template and merge checklist
nodes.rationale: Why matters more than what since the diff already says what. Baseline is pnpm check; anything that can fail silently needs a doctor() check naming the fix; no personal tokens/hostnames in the diff; docs updated when a command, config key or path changes; British English with no em dashes.

nodes.label: Marketing site README (parlour.vercel.app)
nodes.rationale: One HTML file, one stylesheet, no build step. Vercel serves the directory as is, so a change is live on the next push to main and every PR gets a preview. index.html for words, styles.css for looks, vercel.json only adds security headers and clean URLs.

nodes.label: Release 0.1.0: first public release
nodes.rationale: Extracted from a private Home Assistant configuration. Introduces the parlour package (ports, provider registry loading third-party providers from npm, built-in providers ffmpeg, afplay, openWakeWord, whisper.cpp, Kokoro, macOS say, OpenAI-compatible models, Anthropic, SearXNG, Brave; Home Assistant, MCP and connectors integrations), the CLI, the network server, the menu bar app that only drives the CLI, and config moved to ~/.config/parlour/config.json with a provider name in every slot. parlour init converts an old agent.config.json; PARLOUR_TOKEN replaces AGENT_TOKEN (still read this release); /v1/models reports model id parlour.

nodes.label: Changelog (Keep a Changelog, SemVer)
nodes.rationale: Written by hand; format follows Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and versions follow Semantic Versioning.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md graphify rules
nodes.rationale: Instructs the agent to run graphify query/path/explain before grep for codebase questions, use graphify-out/wiki/index.md for navigation, read GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad review, and run graphify update . after modifying code (AST-only, no API cost).

nodes.label: Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct
nodes.rationale: Adapted from Contributor Covenant 2.1 with spelling changed to British English. Reports go to michael@stuntdouble.io.

nodes.label: Mozilla code of conduct enforcement ladder (external)
nodes.norm_label: mozilla code of conduct enforcement ladder (external)

nodes.label: Contributing guide
nodes.rationale: Parlour started as one person's house made general; the most helpful contributions make it work in somebody else's house: a provider for a different engine, an integration for a different platform, Linux. A new voice or STT engine is a self-contained afternoon.

nodes.label: Documentation index (docs/ pages)
nodes.rationale: docs/architecture.md (ports, provider registry, session state machine), docs/providers.md (writing a provider or integration as an npm package), docs/clients.md (satellites, phone page, hardware, /ask, Bonjour), docs/home-assistant.md (MCP Server integration, OpenAI Conversation integration, muting, migration), docs/desktop.md (menu bar app), docs/tuning.md (false wakes), docs/wake-word.md (training your own wake word).

nodes.label: Security policy
nodes.rationale: Parlour holds a token that can control a house, keeps API keys and listens on the network. Report privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting; response within a week, fix or plan within a month. Only the latest release is supported: pre-1.0, fixes go into the next release rather than being backported. Out of scope: security of Home Assistant, LM Studio, whisper.cpp or other services, and anything needing the attacker to already hold the token or a shell.

nodes.label: Tauri generate_context! ordering constraint
nodes.rationale: Tauri's generate_context! macro embeds the frontend and the app icon at compile time and panics when either is missing, so cargo check must come after the nx build (which writes apps/desktop/dist) and after icon generation from src-tauri/icon.png, which is not checked in.

nodes.label: Tag must match package.json version
nodes.rationale: A tag that does not match the version in packages/parlour/package.json would publish the wrong thing under the right name, which npm will not let anyone undo; the job fails and tells you to run pnpm version:set, commit, and tag that commit.

nodes.label: npm trusted publishing via OIDC
nodes.rationale: npm trusts this workflow through the OIDC token, so there is no NPM_TOKEN to rotate or leak; the package settings on npmjs.com name this repository and this file as the trusted publisher. Requires npm 11.5.1 or later, hence npm install -g npm@latest before publish. Provenance records which workflow and commit built the tarball.

nodes.label: Deliberate release follow-ups: unsigned app, no Homebrew tap
nodes.norm_label: deliberate release follow-ups: unsigned app, no homebrew tap
nodes.rationale: The app is unsigned and not notarised, so Gatekeeper asks the person to allow it on first open; signing needs an Apple Developer certificate in repository secrets and tauri-action or xcrun notarytool. No Homebrew tap: npm install -g parlour is the install path and the app is a plain .dmg download until a cask is worth maintaining.

nodes.label: Doctor checks instead of unit tests for hardware/model/network providers
nodes.norm_label: doctor checks instead of unit tests for hardware/model/network providers
nodes.rationale: Providers that need hardware, a model or a network are not unit tested; each has a doctor() instead, and that is the part worth getting right. If the doctor cannot see it, it will break silently: a provider that depends on a binary, a file or a port checks for it in doctor() and says what to do about it.

nodes.label: PARLOUR_HOME scratch install and --no-service
nodes.rationale: PARLOUR_HOME keeps an experiment's config and secrets away from the real ones, but LaunchAgents are one per user, not per home: io.parlour.agent and io.parlour.whisper would be replaced by ones starting the checkout against the scratch directory, which is why init is run with --no-service. PARLOUR_SKIP_MODELS=1 skips the gigabyte of models. Recovery: parlour service uninstall then parlour init from the real install.

nodes.label: Node type stripping constraint (no enums, parameter properties or decorators)
nodes.norm_label: node type stripping constraint (no enums, parameter properties or decorators)
nodes.rationale: The source runs under Node's type stripping, which erases types and nothing else, so TypeScript features that emit runtime code (enums, parameter properties, decorators) are banned.

nodes.label: Native dependency build allowlist (nx, onnxruntime-node, protobufjs, sharp)
nodes.norm_label: native dependency build allowlist (nx, onnxruntime-node, protobufjs, sharp)
nodes.rationale: onnxruntime is the wake word and the voice; sharp and protobufjs come along with them. pnpm blocks install scripts unless they are named here and stopped reading the list from package.json in version 10. Both allowBuilds (current spelling) and onlyBuiltDependencies (older) are listed so whichever pnpm is on the machine agrees.

nodes.label: Cloud escalation: text only, decided per question by the local model
nodes.norm_label: cloud escalation: text only, decided per question by the local model
nodes.rationale: Claude is called only when the local model says it is out of its depth, and receives only the sentence that was said, never the audio. Privacy is the design intent: no account, no server in the middle.

nodes.label: What Parlour does not do, on purpose
nodes.norm_label: what parlour does not do, on purpose
nodes.rationale: Does not tell voices apart (everyone is the same user). Does not cancel its own echo, which is why barge-in is off by default. Does not fail over: one server, satellites wait for it rather than electing a new one, because a house with two brains that disagree is worse than a house with none. No per-person connectors: tokens belong to the household because a satellite cannot tell who is talking. No Linux yet: service manager, secret store and audio sit behind interfaces so it is a contribution rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: PARLOUR_TOKEN gates network exposure
nodes.rationale: All clients need PARLOUR_TOKEN. Without it the server only listens on loopback and does not advertise itself over Bonjour, because a voice assistant on an open port can turn the heating on and read your shopping list.

nodes.label: Every stage is a provider behind a small interface
nodes.norm_label: every stage is a provider behind a small interface
nodes.rationale: Each pipeline stage is a provider chosen by name in a single config file. Built-in choices are the fastest found for Apple silicon; anything else is an npm package away (docs/providers.md).

nodes.label: buildAgent assembly
nodes.rationale: The mic loop, text REPL, doctor and network server all take one Agent rather than building their own, so a timer set from a phone still sounds in the room and every client shares one tool list. A provider that cannot start (missing key) is reported by the doctor and left out, but a name that leads nowhere is thrown, because a house that quietly answers with the wrong model is worse than one that refuses to start.

nodes.label: Kokoro 82M ONNX voice
nodes.rationale: Close to a cloud voice, runs in process, and has British voices. macOS say is the fallback for when it fails.

nodes.label: defineProvider (identity function for inference)
nodes.rationale: Exists so T is inferred and a package's default export reads as what it is.

nodes.label: parlour-tts-piper worked example
nodes.rationale: Renders to a temp file rather than stdout so a stray log line from piper cannot end up inside the WAV. Throwing from render is how a voice fails; core's FallbackTextToSpeech handles it so the provider needs no fallback of its own.

nodes.label: Task 3: config schema and legacy migration
nodes.norm_label: task 3: config schema and legacy migration

nodes.label: Task 9: VoiceSession, agent assembly, testing fakes
nodes.norm_label: task 9: voicesession, agent assembly, testing fakes

nodes.label: tts settings (voice, speed, fallback)
nodes.rationale: Kokoro British voices bf_emma, bf_isabella, bm_george, bm_lewis. An unknown voice falls through to the fallback and the log lists every voice. Kokoro downloads itself on first start so the fallback may speak until it is ready.

nodes.label: Parlour as a library (defineProvider default export)
nodes.norm_label: parlour as a library (defineprovider default export)

nodes.label: config.json Zod schema with defaults for every key
nodes.norm_label: config.json zod schema with defaults for every key
nodes.rationale: Every key has a default, so an empty file is a complete config and parlour config show prints what is in force.

nodes.label: FallbackTextToSpeech
nodes.rationale: Wraps two voices, uses the second when the first throws, warns once and retries the first on the next sentence. Default fallback is macos-say so a Kokoro that has not finished downloading still speaks. Lives in core, not inside the Kokoro provider.

nodes.label: Speaker (TTS + sink + sentence splitting)
nodes.rationale: Composed in core rather than left to a provider. The reply is rendered and played one sentence at a time so the first words come out while the rest is still being made.

nodes.label: Timers in core
nodes.rationale: The one tool that has to keep working when the network does not, so it lives in core and announces through the Speaker.

nodes.label: Migration from agent.config.json
nodes.rationale: parlour init looks for agent.config.json in cwd and offers to convert: homeAssistant.* to integrations['home-assistant'], mcpServers to integrations.mcp.servers, search.searxngUrl to search.url, tts.engine say to macos-say, .env to secrets.env with AGENT_TOKEN renamed to PARLOUR_TOKEN. AGENT_TOKEN stays a fallback for one release so upgrading does not lock every phone and satellite out. The old default mute entity input_boolean.home_agent_muted is written out so the mute keeps working.

nodes.label: parlour/testing fakes for every port
nodes.rationale: Each fake records what it was asked so a provider can run through the same VoiceSession and Router the built-ins are tested against. Providers needing hardware or a model are not unit tested; each has a doctor() instead, which is what a person sees when the thing does not work.

nodes.label: History preserved via git subtree split of agent/
nodes.norm_label: history preserved via git subtree split of agent/
nodes.rationale: The nine agent/ commits from the Home Assistant config repository are kept; nothing is pushed to GitHub until the owner says so.

nodes.label: Paths (PARLOUR_HOME, PARLOUR_CONFIG, caches, logs, XDG on Linux)
nodes.norm_label: paths (parlour_home, parlour_config, caches, logs, xdg on linux)

nodes.label: HA_TOKEN long-lived access token
nodes.rationale: That token is the whole house, so it stays in secrets.env with mode 600 and never near git.

nodes.label: Task 2: ports, provider registry, paths, secrets
nodes.norm_label: task 2: ports, provider registry, paths, secrets

nodes.label: search settings (searxng, brave, none)
nodes.rationale: Only the local model uses this; the cloud model brings its own search. SearXNG needs json under search.formats.

nodes.label: Quick start (npm install -g parlour; init; text; start)
nodes.norm_label: quick start (npm install -g parlour; init; text; start)
nodes.rationale: Needs a Mac with Node 22 and Homebrew; init fetches ffmpeg, whisper.cpp and the models through brew.

nodes.label: core/builtins.ts as the only core-to-providers import
nodes.norm_label: core/builtins.ts as the only core-to-providers import
nodes.rationale: Nothing in core imports providers except builtins.ts, which only registers the built-ins; a program embedding Parlour with its own providers can leave that one file out.

nodes.label: Ports (core/ports.ts seams)
nodes.rationale: Each port interface is kept small enough to fake in a test and to fill from an npm package; they are the seams between the pure core and anything that touches hardware, a model or the network.

nodes.label: Provider registry keyed by (kind, name)
nodes.rationale: Core only knows the provider key of each config slice; the rest passes through to the provider's own Zod schema so core has no idea Kokoro has a voice. An unregistered name is tried as an npm package via await import(name), which is the entire extension mechanism. secrets and service are picked by platform rather than config.

nodes.label: secrets.env (mode 600, env wins)
nodes.rationale: HA_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, PARLOUR_TOKEN, BRAVE_API_KEY, LOG_LEVEL stay in secrets.env with mode 600; the process environment wins over the file so a one-off run can override without editing.

nodes.label: apiKeyEnv pattern: name the variable, not the value
nodes.norm_label: apikeyenv pattern: name the variable, not the value
nodes.rationale: context.secrets is a closed set; a provider with its own key takes the env variable's name as an option because parlour copies secrets.env into process.env before any command. Keeps keys out of config.json, lets people rename, and makes parlour secrets status list it. Report a missing key from doctor() rather than throwing in create.

nodes.label: type: module and parlour as peer dependency
nodes.norm_label: type: module and parlour as peer dependency
nodes.rationale: Parlour loads packages with import(), and a CommonJS default export is not module.exports. parlour is a peer dependency because the definition is imported from it and there must be exactly one copy. Against a checkout, a file: devDependency satisfies the peer and the link must stay in place at run time because the import is real.

nodes.label: secrets and service picked by platform
nodes.norm_label: secrets and service picked by platform
nodes.rationale: Not named in config; adding a systemd ServiceManager means registering it in providers/service/index.ts, which makes it a pull request rather than a package.

nodes.label: resolveProvider: how a name becomes a running thing
nodes.norm_label: resolveprovider: how a name becomes a running thing
nodes.rationale: Registry lookup, then await import(name) (.. refused, absolute paths allowed for trying a checkout), accept default export whose kind matches, register under the config name, parse options with the schema, call create. Only 'nothing there' is reported as unknown with alternatives listed; a package that exists but fails to load is reported as exactly that. Context can be a function of the definition so a provider tried by absolute path still logs as its own name.
nodes.source_location: ## How a name becomes a running thing

nodes.label: macOS server and menu bar app first; Linux as a contribution path
nodes.norm_label: macos server and menu bar app first; linux as a contribution path
nodes.rationale: Platform specifics sit behind interfaces so Linux is a contribution path, not a deliverable. Linux, Docker, speaker identification, echo cancellation, signing and a Homebrew tap are out of scope.

nodes.label: One publishable package plus desktop app (approach C)
nodes.norm_label: one publishable package plus desktop app (approach c)
nodes.rationale: Not a package per provider. Built-in providers are moves of existing classes, not rewrites; third parties extend via npm packages.

nodes.label: Phone page index.html (push to talk)
nodes.rationale: A minimal PWA shell (manifest, apple-mobile-web-app-capable, theme-color) with a settings section for the token and room, a transcript showing heard and reply, a hold-to-talk button and a status line; behaviour lives in app.js and styling in app.css.

nodes.label: Endpointer
nodes.rationale: Gives up after 2.5 s of leading silence, finishes after audio.silenceMs of quiet once speech has started, caps a request at audio.maxUtteranceMs.

nodes.label: Bonjour advertisement _parlour._tcp
nodes.rationale: TXT record says role=server, token=required|none, api=/v1. Name is discovery.name or '<config.name> on <hostname>'. discovery.enabled false means every satellite needs serverUrl filled in.

nodes.label: /listen WebSocket (wake mode and push mode)
nodes.rationale: Send 16 kHz mono s16 PCM in binary frames of any size; the server re-cuts to 80 ms frames. Wake mode runs the server's own openWakeWord and endpointing so hardware can be just a mic, speaker and network stack. Push mode (&mode=push) uses start/end/cancel messages for a button or hardware with its own wake word. {type:spoke} lets the server resume listening immediately after playback.

nodes.label: Phone push-to-talk page (/ and POST /voice)
nodes.rationale: Posts one recording to POST /voice?client=phone&room=kitchen and gets { heard, reply, via, audio } with a base64 WAV. A ?token=...&room= link fills in settings so nothing is typed on a phone keyboard. Safari only grants microphone over HTTPS or localhost, so iOS needs a reverse proxy or Tailscale.

nodes.label: audio settings (inputDevice, silenceMs, silenceThreshold, maxUtteranceMs, bargeIn)
nodes.norm_label: audio settings (inputdevice, silencems, silencethreshold, maxutterancems, bargein)
nodes.rationale: silenceThreshold is an RMS level 0 to 1; a noisy room wants it higher, a quiet speaker lower. maxUtteranceMs is a safety net for a microphone that never goes quiet rather than a way to allow long questions.

nodes.label: Per-client sessions keyed by client id
nodes.norm_label: per-client sessions keyed by client id
nodes.rationale: Every client has its own session so a follow-up in the kitchen cannot pick up something asked in the study; history is forgotten after four minutes of silence.

nodes.label: Voice session state machine (idle/listening/thinking/speaking)
nodes.rationale: One state machine over a stream of 80 ms frames that does not care where frames come from: local mic, satellite, phone or custom hardware all feed the same object. Frames arriving while speaking reset the wake word instead of being listened to unless audio.bargeIn is on, because with one box in one room the microphone hears the speaker. Clients that know their own request boundaries call utterance(frames) and skip wake and endpointing.

nodes.label: POST /ask for automations
nodes.rationale: JSON content type is required because a web form can post text/plain anywhere without the browser asking first but cannot claim to be JSON (CSRF defence). Returns { reply, via }; callers without a client id share the api session.

nodes.label: PARLOUR_TOKEN and loopback-only default
nodes.rationale: Without a token the server only listens on loopback and does not advertise, because a voice assistant on an open port can turn the heating on and read your shopping list. A browser on the same machine addressed by a name other than localhost counts as somewhere else. Token is sent as Authorization: Bearer or ?token= for the socket and phone page; secrets set reads from stdin so it never lands in shell history.

nodes.label: Satellite role
nodes.rationale: Any Mac with Node, ffmpeg and the parlour package; no models, keys or GPU. It finds the server by Bonjour once and pins the address in serverUrl thereafter, because anything on the network can advertise _parlour._tcp and the satellite hands its token to whatever it connects to, so the first server it trusts is the only one it trusts. Backs off up to satellite.retryMs when the server is down. Plays the server's speech so the voice is the same in every room.

nodes.label: HA as a client via OpenAI Conversation (/v1, model parlour)
nodes.norm_label: ha as a client via openai conversation (/v1, model parlour)
nodes.rationale: Home Assistant and every Voice PE satellite keep doing wake word, STT and speech back; only the thinking moves to Parlour. The prompt and temperature on the HA page are ignored because Parlour brings its own persona and tools. Each HA user gets a conversation of their own.

nodes.label: ffmpeg on avfoundation capture
nodes.rationale: Nothing to compile, and the only reliable way to pin one input device on macOS.

nodes.norm_label: lib/bridge.ts, the only caller of invoke()

nodes.label: bin/parlour-dev for running the CLI from source
nodes.norm_label: bin/parlour-dev for running the cli from source

nodes.label: App settings.json (parlourBin, autostart)
nodes.rationale: The app's only two facts. The path is kept as long as it is executable so the app will not swap a checkout's parlour-dev back for the global copy.

nodes.label: supervisor.rs (parlour start --events child)
nodes.rationale: Stopping sends SIGINT rather than SIGKILL, because Parlour shuts ffmpeg down on it and an orphaned ffmpeg would keep hold of the microphone.

nodes.label: Task 12: the desktop app drives the CLI
nodes.norm_label: task 12: the desktop app drives the cli

nodes.label: CLI surface (init, start, text, doctor, service, connectors, models, config, secrets)
nodes.norm_label: cli surface (init, start, text, doctor, service, connectors, models, config, secrets)
nodes.rationale: init has two halves: setup.ts with no questions and the questions; --porcelain prints one JSON line per event for the app; --yes takes every default and stops only for the secrets.

nodes.label: Wake model input: last 16 speech embeddings
nodes.norm_label: wake model input: last 16 speech embeddings
nodes.rationale: The provider feeds each word the last 16 speech embeddings; notebook-trained models for a few-syllable phrase expect exactly that, and onnxruntime-node can print a model's input and output names to check.

nodes.label: parlour doctor (concatenated Check[])
nodes.rationale: Every configured part's doctor() checks joined together, plus three of core's own: config parses, the network is let in, something keeps Parlour running.

nodes.label: App and LaunchAgent are alternatives, not a pair
nodes.norm_label: app and launchagent are alternatives, not a pair
nodes.rationale: Two copies of Parlour means two processes fighting over one microphone and one port, so parlour init sets up only one and the app leaves the agent to itself.

nodes.label: main.rs generic parlour(args, stdin) command
nodes.rationale: The Rust side knows the path to the parlour binary and nothing else; config, secrets, doctor and connectors all go through the CLI's --json and stdin interfaces.

nodes.label: Microphone permission belongs to whatever starts it
nodes.norm_label: microphone permission belongs to whatever starts it
nodes.rationale: macOS grants the mic to the responsible process, which for anything the app spawns is the app. Onboarding opens the device briefly to trigger the prompt; the bundle carries NSMicrophoneUsageDescription or macOS refuses rather than asks. A LaunchAgent is a separate grant.

nodes.label: Tauri menu bar app drives the CLI
nodes.norm_label: tauri menu bar app drives the cli
nodes.rationale: An interface rather than a second implementation: everything it knows about Parlour it learns by running the CLI, and every setting it writes goes through parlour config write, so the app and the terminal can never disagree about the same house. It does not bundle Node or the package because one copy of Parlour is better than two that can disagree.

nodes.label: Global constraints (Node 22 type stripping, .ts imports, node:test, British English)
nodes.norm_label: global constraints (node 22 type stripping, .ts imports, node:test, british english)
nodes.rationale: Dev runs source with node --experimental-strip-types and tsc compiles dist; erasableSyntaxOnly means no enums, parameter properties or decorators. Tests sit beside source with no framework dependency. No references to the old home-agent names may remain except in migration code.

nodes.label: Home Assistant integration (tools, prompt line, mute gate)
nodes.norm_label: home assistant integration (tools, prompt line, mute gate)
nodes.rationale: Parlour's first integration, on by default under integrations['home-assistant'] with url, mcp, rest and muteEntity.

nodes.label: REST escape hatches ha_get_state and ha_call_service
nodes.norm_label: rest escape hatches ha_get_state and ha_call_service
nodes.rationale: For what intents cannot express; the prompt tells the model to prefer a more specific tool when one fits.
nodes.source_location: ## What Parlour can do with it

nodes.label: Task 7: integrations and the secret store
nodes.norm_label: task 7: integrations and the secret store

nodes.label: --events NDJSON stream (ready, state, heard, reply, muted, error)
nodes.norm_label: --events ndjson stream (ready, state, heard, reply, muted, error)
nodes.rationale: One JSON line per state change on stdout so the desktop app draws its status from structured events rather than scraping log text.

nodes.label: One server, everything else is a client
nodes.norm_label: one server, everything else is a client
nodes.rationale: One machine runs the models, holds the tokens and answers; every other microphone sends what it hears and plays what it is sent, running no models. The server's own microphone is one client among these with no special privileges.

nodes.label: HA Model Context Protocol Server (/mcp_server/sse)
nodes.rationale: Publishes whatever is exposed under Settings > Voice assistants > Expose as tools, so Parlour inherits it all with nothing to change on its side. If the MCP connection fails the REST tools remain, so the house is still reachable the slower way.
nodes.source_location: ## What Parlour can do with it

nodes.label: muteEntity gate (fails open)
nodes.rationale: Parlour asks over REST after the wake word fires and before it acts, so the mute is enforced by the house rather than by the machine and covers every client alike. If the house cannot be reached the gate reads as off: a house that cannot be asked should still be able to hear you. A muted wake emits a muted event so the desktop app can explain why nothing happened.

nodes.label: defineTool and short tool names
nodes.rationale: Every tool description sits in the local model's context on every turn, so a package with forty tools makes every answer slower; keep names stable and short.

nodes.label: Integration interface (tools, promptContext, gate, close)
nodes.rationale: Selected by being a key under integrations; the block replaces the default rather than adding, so a hand-written one must keep home-assistant and connectors. tools() is called once at assembly so a connection opened there stays open; close() shuts it.

nodes.label: Injectable fetch, clock and setTimeout for testability
nodes.norm_label: injectable fetch, clock and settimeout for testability
nodes.rationale: The HA gate takes options.fetch, the Router takes now(), Timers take setTimeout, and resolvePaths reads HOME from its env argument, so each can be tested without a network, real time or the host's home directory.

nodes.label: Claude with server-side web search as escalation
nodes.norm_label: claude with server-side web search as escalation
nodes.rationale: The local model is fast and private but wrong more often. Handing over is cheap; being wrong out loud is not.
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces

nodes.label: LM Studio MLX local model over OpenAI API
nodes.norm_label: lm studio mlx local model over openai api
nodes.rationale: Fastest way to run an 8B model on Apple silicon, and it speaks the OpenAI API so the runtime stays swappable.
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces

nodes.label: whisper.cpp small.en kept warm as a server
nodes.norm_label: whisper.cpp small.en kept warm as a server
nodes.rationale: Loading the model costs more than transcribing a sentence, so it runs as a server (a separate LaunchAgent, io.parlour.whisper).

nodes.label: Task 6: LLM and search providers, loop and router
nodes.norm_label: task 6: llm and search providers, loop and router

nodes.label: llm settings (local, cloud, maxToolRounds)
nodes.rationale: A model that regularly exceeds local.timeoutMs is too big for the machine and with onLocalFailure every timeout becomes a slower, non-private cloud answer. cloud.enabled false keeps everything local and drops the escalation tool. Six tool rounds is enough for 'turn the kitchen and hall lights off and set a timer'. How often the cloud is asked is decided by the prompt, not a threshold.

nodes.label: Each stage chosen to be fast rather than best
nodes.norm_label: each stage chosen to be fast rather than best
nodes.rationale: Latency adds up across wake, capture, STT, model, speech, so every stage is picked for speed; the cloud model is the safety net for correctness. Being wrong out loud is expensive; handing over is cheap.
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces

nodes.label: Router (local first, cloud escalation)
nodes.rationale: The local model gets the prompt, the tools and ask_the_clever_one; when it calls it, the rewritten question and history go to the cloud model, which has server-side web search and no house tools. If local throws or times out and llm.cloud.onLocalFailure is true, cloud gets the original question. With no cloud model, failures are final and the escalation tool is not offered.

nodes.label: Tool rounds loop (core/loop.ts)
nodes.rationale: Runs the tool rounds for whichever model is answering, up to llm.maxToolRounds, and stops with an apology rather than looping forever.

nodes.label: Dark Charcoal and Mint Green Palette
nodes.norm_label: dark charcoal and mint green palette

nodes.label: openWakeWord (ONNX, in process)
nodes.rationale: Free, offline, and runs in the same Node process as everything else, which is what makes barge-in possible.
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces

nodes.label: wake settings (words, threshold, refractoryMs)
nodes.rationale: Stock words hey_jarvis, alexa, hey_mycroft; any openWakeWord .onnx dropped into the models directory works. Raise threshold towards 0.7 for television false wakes, lower towards 0.4 if deaf; raise refractoryMs if it fires twice.

nodes.label: openWakeWord automatic_model_training.ipynb (full notebook)
nodes.rationale: Two extra levers matter more than the numbers: target_phrase takes a list of spellings and custom_negative_phrases takes sound-alikes that should not fire.

nodes.label: satellite.localWake
nodes.rationale: Runs the wake word on the satellite and streams only what follows; costs a copy of the models on that machine and saves a constant 32 KB/s. Off by default because it is one less thing to keep in step.

nodes.label: Training a custom openWakeWord model
nodes.rationale: An hour on a free Colab GPU; the provider is the same three-stage pipeline for every word so a new word is a new .onnx file and one line of config. Spell target_word as 'hey parlor' because Piper synthesises the training clips and reads spellings literally; the model learns the sound. 2000 examples and 20000 steps tighten it noticeably over the defaults.

nodes.label: false_activation_penalty vs threshold
nodes.rationale: Custom models score a little lower than stock ones so threshold can come down to 0.4. If it wakes for the room, raise false_activation_penalty and retrain rather than pushing threshold past 0.7, which mostly makes it deaf to you as well.

nodes.label: Listening Ripple Motif (solid dot radiating a faint concentric ring, evoking a wake-word listener / sound wave)
nodes.norm_label: listening ripple motif (solid dot radiating a faint concentric ring, evoking a wake-word listener / sound wave)

nodes.norm_label: parlour (product the icon represents; svg title and aria-label)

nodes.norm_label: parlour brand identity (deep green #14312b + warm gold #e9b84a)

nodes.label: Parlour Favicon (dark green rounded square, gold dot with translucent ring)
nodes.norm_label: parlour favicon (dark green rounded square, gold dot with translucent ring)

nodes.label: Icons generated from src-tauri/icon.png
nodes.rationale: Only icon.png is in git; the source sits outside icons/ because tauri icon writes an icon.png into its output and a source kept there would rewrite itself on every build.

nodes.label: No Tauri plugins, capability list core:default
nodes.norm_label: no tauri plugins, capability list core:default
nodes.rationale: Everything the app does happens in Rust where it can be reasoned about. Activation policy Accessory: no Dock icon, tray is the way back, closing the window leaves Parlour running.
